description: Cross-engine parity corpus for test/matcher-parity.test.mjs. Compares screen.py against scripts/sanctions-match.mjs ENGINE TO ENGINE, which no other test does — the accuracy benchmarks measure each backend against its own floor and test/benchmark_eval.py states outright that 'the two are NOT comparable'. Both historical parity failures (Turkish dotless i, two-letter name tokens) were silent JS-side FALSE NEGATIVES invisible to those per-backend floors. Every name here is synthetic or a well-known public designation used as a matching fixture; no customer data.
names_note: Grouped: Turkish-i regression class; diacritic Latin that MUST fold to A-Z; short/two-letter token class (the sigTokens regression); transliteration-variant class; lost-script class (Cyrillic/Arabic/CJK/Greek and unfoldable Latin) which both engines must FLAG rather than silently clear; and degenerate inputs (blank, symbols, digits, single char).

pairs.subject: Kılıç
pairs.why: Turkish dotless i must fold identically in both engines (historical JS false negative)

pairs.subject: Yu Li Pang
pairs.why: two-letter name tokens must reach the candidate index in both engines (historical JS false negative)

pairs.subject: Xi Da Wai
pairs.why: all-short-token transliterated name with one long token

pairs.subject: Müller
pairs.why: diacritic Latin folds to A-Z in both engines

pairs.subject: Sterling Bullion FZE
pairs.why: corporate-suffix stripping leaves the distinctive core in both engines

pairs.subject: Hamas General Trading LLC
pairs.why: short designation + legal-form boilerplate: full=33 drags min() under the near-exact gate while the distinctive core is exact — screened CLEAR in screen.py until 2026-07-29 while the JS engine scored it 100/critical

pairs.subject: Al Qaeda General Trading
pairs.why: long entry whose distinctive core is ONE token (AL is a particle), so neither the min() gate (full=50) nor the subset gate (needs >=2 core tokens) could fire — also the score-tie that made screening depend on the process hash seed

pairs.subject: Weiss Trading
pairs.why: German sharp-s: ß has no NFKD decomposition and lower-casing leaves it, so the JS engine normalized it apart from the universal ss spelling and cleared a designation screen.py scored 100 — the same silent-JS-false-negative class as the Turkish ı and two-letter-token regressions

pairs.subject: ХАМАС
pairs.why: Cyrillic subject vs Latin designation. screen.py romanizes to KHAMAS; this engine kept Cyrillic (хамас) and could never match the Latin entry — Python would hit, JS would not, breaking the directional parity contract.

pairs.subject: Калашников Концерн
pairs.why: Cyrillic corporate designation against its Latin rendering — the shape that dominates current Russia-related OFAC/EU/UK listings.

pairs.subject: Ɔla
pairs.why: African-Latin hook letter Ɔ must fold to O in BOTH engines (JS false negative before the ɔ fold added 2026-08-05)

pairs.subject: Ɖamir
pairs.why: African-Latin Ɖ must fold to D in both engines

pairs_note: Every pair is a TRUE match that both engines must reach. The invariant is engine-to-engine agreement on reachability, not score equality: rapidfuzz and the JS Levenshtein legitimately differ by a point or two (measured: 93 vs 94 on Muhammad Alfayed), so the test asserts both engines HIT, never that they score the same.
